narrativeReportMd:
# Questionnaire R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps `Questionnaire` as the same concrete resource, but it has several local breaking changes. The highest-impact change is the required `Questionnaire.item.type` binding: R4 `choice`, `open-choice`, and `question` are no longer usable R6 item types, and R6 adds `coding` plus `answerConstraint` for coded-answer semantics.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions and supporting local terminology artifacts. Inherited Resource, DomainResource, Element, and Extension changes were excluded from findings.

## Main migration themes
The main migration themes are: item-type and subject-type code migration; stricter local invariants for linkId, enableWhen, answer options, initial values, answerValueSet, and maxLength; R6-only elements and choice types that cannot be represented in R4; and summary serialization changes for local Questionnaire metadata.

## Highest-impact findings
The most important findings are `Questionnaire:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Questionnaire.item.type:item-type-useable`, `Questionnaire:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Questionnaire.subjectType:resource-types`, and `Questionnaire:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Questionnaire.item.answerConstraint:added`. Together they affect validation, renderer behavior, code generation, and lossless R6-to-R4 conversion.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for mapping `choice`/`open-choice`/`question`, mapping removed resource-type codes in `subjectType`, fixing comparator-bearing quantities, choosing missing `enableBehavior`, and deciding how to preserve value-set or maxLength semantics.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many R6 changes are semantically justified, but several could have been staged with deprecated codes or warning invariants. Required binding code removal and hard validation invariants are the main sources of old-valid/new-invalid breaks.

## Follow-up analysis
Review QuestionnaireResponse, resource-type cross-version maps, SimpleQuantity/Quantity, and inherited Resource/DomainResource reports before publishing a complete migration guide.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Questionnaire has material local R4-to-R6 breaks, led by item-type code replacement (`choice`/`open-choice`/`question` to `coding` plus `answerConstraint`), changed `subjectType` resource codes, and stricter validation invariants. The largest uncertainty is not the computable diff but the correct business mapping for old coded-answer and subject-type semantics.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Upgrade work should focus on code migrations, invariant repair, and preserving answer semantics. R4 `choice` and `open-choice` should not be mechanically renamed without setting `answerConstraint`; exactly-two `enableWhen` rules need explicit `enableBehavior`; invalid or ambiguous linkIds need coordinated renaming across responses and logic; and R6-only fields/types require extensions or controlled loss when downgrading.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level changes because both assigned definitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for terminology impact details because local CodeSystem/ValueSet definitions were compared without a live terminology expansion or official ballot rationale. The R6 package is a ballot build marked not for publication, so details may change before final publication.

findings.title: Questionnaire.item.type required binding removes choice, open-choice, and question and adds coding

oldState.summary: Required binding to item-type|4.0.1 allowed choice, open-choice, and the generic question code.

binding.description: Distinguishes groups from questions and display text and indicates data type for questions.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Code comparison used the local CodeSystem/ValueSet compose definitions, not a live terminology expansion.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 modelled coded-answer questions with `choice` and `open-choice`, and the required value set also included the generic parent code `question`.

newState.summary: Required binding to item-type-useable|6.0.0-ballot4 excludes question and replaces choice/open-choice with coding plus answerConstraint semantics.

binding.description: Distinguishes groups from questions and display text and indicates data type for questions.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses the concrete `coding` item type and the new `answerConstraint` element to distinguish closed lists, typed extra values, and string "other" answers.

facts.note: These R4 item.type codes are not in the R6 usable value set.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged; the required binding target and underlying code inventory changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct required-binding validation break. R4 Questionnaires with `item.type` = `choice`, `open-choice`, or `question` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6. Conversely, R6 Questionnaires using `coding` are not valid R4 without a lossy or extension-based representation. Generated enums and switch statements over item type also need updates.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Wrongly migrating coded-answer controls can change whether free-text "other" answers are accepted, which can affect data capture and downstream extraction.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace ambiguous choice/open-choice/question item types with a concrete answer datatype and a separate answer-constraint mechanism.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep choice, open-choice, and question as legacy or deprecated codes while adding coding and answerConstraint.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: coded-answer datatype and open/closed answer semantics are clearer when `coding` and `answerConstraint` are separate. The break is still material because a required binding invalidates common R4 `choice` and `open-choice` instances. A legacy-code path could reduce the break, but the duplicate semantics and ambiguous `question` code make the R6 breaking design probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the R4 `choice`, `open-choice`, and possibly `question` codes in the R6 required value set as deprecated legacy codes while adding `coding` and `answerConstraint`. That would keep many R4 questionnaires valid. The cost is that renderers, validators, and authors would need to support both old encoded semantics and the new normalized representation indefinitely, and `question` still would not identify a concrete answer datatype.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves many old forms but leaves duplicate coded-answer representations and keeps the generic question code ambiguous.

evidence.detail: R4 binds item.type required to item-type|4.0.1.
R6 binds item.type required to item-type-useable|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local terminology comparison found removed R4 codes choice, open-choice, question and added R6 code coding.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments are illustrative and omit unrelated metadata. `question` has no safe automatic R6 equivalent; it needs manual selection of a concrete datatype.

findings.narrativeMd: `Questionnaire.item.type` is the highest-impact Questionnaire-local change. Existing R4 forms frequently use `choice` and `open-choice`; in R6 those codes are gone from the required binding and the new `coding` code is used instead. The open/closed nature of the answer list moved out of the type code into `answerConstraint`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validators should reject old `choice`, `open-choice`, and `question` codes under the R6 required binding. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot serialize `coding` as a valid R4 code without mapping to `choice`/`open-choice` and possibly losing the exact `answerConstraint` semantics. Runtime code using generated item-type enums must handle both removed and added codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `choice` to `coding` with `answerConstraint=optionsOnly` when the R4 questionnaire intended answers to come only from the enumerated list. Map `open-choice` to `coding` with `answerConstraint=optionsOrString`, and preserve `maxLength` only if that answerConstraint is present. Review any use of generic `question` manually and replace it with the actual answer datatype.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive by retaining deprecated aliases in the R6 required value set. The R6 approach is semantically cleaner, but because the binding is required, code removal is a true validation break rather than a soft deprecation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The migration recipe depends on whether the R4 form treated choices as closed. If local profiles or renderer conventions allowed answers outside `choice`, manual review is needed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The binding change is a real front-door break: R4 questionnaires that used `choice` or `open-choice` for coded answer questions no longer satisfy the R6 required value set, and migration must also choose the right `answerConstraint`. Because these codes are central to ordinary questionnaire authoring, one-step removal deserves design review even though the R6 `coding` plus `answerConstraint` model is cleaner.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.item.type required binding is ValueSet-item-type|4.0.1; R6 binding is ValueSet-item-type-useable|6.0.0-ballot4.
R4 CodeSystem-item-type includes choice and open-choice; R6 CodeSystem-item-type replaces those with coding and ValueSet-item-type-useable excludes question.
R6 questionnaire-answer-constraint CodeSystem defines optionsOnly, optionsOrType, and optionsOrString.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Questionnaire is R4 FMM 3/trial-use. That is not normative, but this is a central discriminator in a mature resource, so common required-binding removals need stronger justification.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 type=choice, type=open-choice, or type=question instances can fail R6 validation; generated enums and R6-to-R4 mappings also need explicit translation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could retain choice and open-choice as deprecated legacy codes with defined mapping to coding plus answerConstraint. That creates duplicate representations, but it appears feasible enough for such a central path to merit revisit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact assessment and partial alternative judgment; I give the alternative more weight because deprecated legacy codes could preserve many R4 forms.

findings.title: Questionnaire.subjectType required resource-type binding changed with R6 resource inventory

oldState.summary: Required binding to R4 resource-types allowed the R4 resource inventory, including resources later removed or renamed.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `subjectType` values were drawn from the R4 `resource-types` CodeSystem.

newState.summary: Required binding points to the R6 ballot resource-types value set, with removed R4 resource codes and new R6 resource codes.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `subjectType` is constrained to the R6 resource inventory. Several R4 resource names no longer validate, and new R6 names cannot be represented in R4.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path is unchanged; only the required value set version/content changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is required, an R4 Questionnaire whose `subjectType` names an R4-only resource such as `DeviceUseStatement` or `MedicationKnowledge` is invalid against R6. R6-only subject types such as `DeviceAssociation` or `RequestOrchestration` cannot be represented as valid R4 codes.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subject type drives whether QuestionnaireResponses are appropriate for a patient, device, practitioner, or other resource. A wrong or dropped mapping can affect workflow routing and validation.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep Questionnaire.subjectType aligned with the version-specific FHIR resource inventory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a union or historical resource-type value set that retains legacy R4 resource codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Keeping `subjectType` aligned with the release-specific resource inventory is a reasonable R6 goal because it lets validators know whether a named subject resource exists in that FHIR version. A less-breaking union value set is possible, but it would weaken that guarantee and would not resolve resource renames, removals, and semantic replacements. Given those material tradeoffs, the required-binding break is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 alternative could have included historical R4 resource-type codes or used a version-independent value set. That would preserve R4 questionnaires that name R4-only subject types. However, it would allow R6 `Questionnaire.subjectType` to name resources that are not valid R6 resources, forcing every validator and workflow engine to understand cross-version resource history. ConceptMaps or extensions help migration but are mitigations, not backwards-compatible base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old subjectType values but permits references to resources not present in R6 and obscures renamed, split, or merged resource semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 subjectType uses resource-types|4.0.1.
R6 subjectType uses resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local code comparison found 41 R4 resource-type codes absent from the R6 value set and 20 R6 codes absent from R4.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments show the binding issue only; a real migration needs an artifact-specific mapping for each removed or added resource code.

findings.narrativeMd: `Questionnaire.subjectType` is local to Questionnaire and has a required binding to resource names. The binding changed along with the R6 resource inventory, so this is a concrete validation issue for questionnaires whose intended response subject used resources removed, renamed, merged, or newly introduced between releases.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs whenever an R4 `subjectType` contains a code not present in the R6 value set. R6-to-R4 conversion has the inverse problem for new R6 resource codes. Strict enum code generators and validators will fail these values rather than treating them as display text.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build an explicit resource-type ConceptMap for questionnaire subject types. Some mappings are plausible renames or replacements, while others require manual business review. Do not silently drop `subjectType`; absence means unrestricted subject type and can materially broaden permitted QuestionnaireResponses.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A version-independent binding would have been easier for cross-version payloads but less precise for a release-specific core resource. Required version-specific resource names are defensible, but migration tooling must handle the changed inventory.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The report did not infer one-to-one mappings for every removed resource name; this should be coordinated with the corresponding resource-level reports.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `subjectType` follows the release-specific resource inventory. A required binding makes R4-only subject resource codes invalid in R6, but allowing historical resource names in the R6 base value set would weaken validation and would not resolve removed, renamed, or semantically replaced resources.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.subjectType required binding is resource-types|4.0.1; R6 binding is resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local value set comparison found 41 R4 resource-type codes absent from R6 and 20 R6-only codes.
The element remains 0..* code in both versions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the compatibility burden, but this binding is tied to version-specific resource identity rather than a Questionnaire-only modeling preference.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Questionnaire naming an R4-only subjectType can fail R6 required-binding validation; R6-only subject types also do not downgrade cleanly.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A union or historical resource-type value set would preserve more R4 instances, but it would permit R6 questionnaires to name resources not present in R6 and would push cross-version resource semantics into every validator.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment, but judge the break proportionate to the release-inventory goal.

findings.title: R6 adds Questionnaire.item.answerConstraint for open or closed answer sets

oldState.summary: No core element represented whether answerOption or answerValueSet was closed, open by type, or open by string.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 encoded open coded choices primarily through `item.type=open-choice`.

newState.summary: Optional code element with required binding to optionsOnly, optionsOrType, and optionsOrString.

binding.description: Indicates modes for restricting values when options or valueset are specified.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates answer datatype (`coding`, `string`, etc.) from the rule that controls whether answers outside the listed options are allowed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not invalidate R4 instances moving forward, but R6 instances that rely on `answerConstraint` cannot be represented in native R4. Ignoring it changes whether unlisted answers are allowed and what datatype those answers may use.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide explicit answer-set openness semantics independent of item.type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding optional answerConstraint does not invalidate R4 Questionnaire instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 needs an explicit way to represent whether listed answers are closed, open by type, or open by string. Because the element is optional, the base R6 design does not make R4-valid questionnaires invalid. The compatibility issue is mainly R6-to-R4 representability, so a backward-compatible alternative judgment is not applicable under the calibration rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility because existing R4 content can omit the new element. A cross-version extension could preserve `answerConstraint` during downgrade to R4, but that is a conversion/backport mitigation, not a backwards-compatible base R6 design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Populated R6 answerConstraint values create downgrade loss, but extensions or backports are mitigations rather than less-breaking R6 base designs.

evidence.detail: R6 adds answerConstraint 0..1 of type code with a required binding.
The R6 code system defines optionsOnly, optionsOrType, and optionsOrString.

examples.examplesMd: In R4, similar behavior may need `open-choice` or an extension, but neither exactly preserves all R6 answerConstraint modes.

findings.narrativeMd: `answerConstraint` is a new semantic control on answer sets. It is especially important because R6 removed `choice` and `open-choice`; systems must now look at both `item.type` and `answerConstraint` to decide whether values outside the listed options are valid.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 instances are not invalidated by the addition. R6-to-R4 instances lose information unless a cross-version extension or local profile is used. Runtime renderers that ignore the element can present the wrong UI or reject/accept the wrong QuestionnaireResponse answers.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When upgrading, populate `answerConstraint` while converting old `choice` and `open-choice` items. When downgrading, map `optionsOnly` to R4 `choice` where possible, map `optionsOrString` to R4 `open-choice` where possible, and represent `optionsOrType` with an extension or manual rule because R4 has no exact core equivalent.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The element could have been introduced as an extension first, but making it core gives validators and renderers a consistent place to find answer-set semantics. The cost is that R6 content using it is not natively R4-representable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `answerConstraint` is an optional new semantic control. It can matter when rendering or downgrading R6 forms, but adding it does not make any R4 Questionnaire invalid; the disruptive migration work is mainly caused by the separate `item.type` redesign.
keyEvidence: R4 has no Questionnaire.item.answerConstraint element.
R6 adds Questionnaire.item.answerConstraint 0..1 code with required binding to questionnaire-answer-constraint.
R6 questionnaire-answer-constraint codes checked locally: optionsOnly, optionsOrType, optionsOrString.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not turn an optional additive element into a forward compatibility concern, though it supports documenting downgrade behavior.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: a populated answerConstraint has no native R4 slot; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism for this added optional element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for forward compatibility. Keeping the concept extension-only would not preserve any R4 instance and would reduce standard renderer interoperability.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing high-impact framing for this finding alone; agree that a less-breaking base alternative is not applicable.

findings.title: Questionnaire.item.definition is repeatable in R6

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed at most one URI pointing to a defining ElementDefinition.

newState.summary: definition remains uri but can repeat.

semanticText.definition: R6 text says the URI can refer to an ElementDefinition or ObservationDefinition.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits multiple definition URIs. The type is still `uri`; the ObservationDefinition reference is a semantic text broadening, not a structural target-profile change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to cardinality, but R6 instances with multiple `item.definition` values cannot be represented losslessly in R4. Generated R4 models often expose a scalar string/URI, while R6 models must expose a list.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow an item to trace to more than one defining source.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: increasing max cardinality preserves R4 instances with zero or one definition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing more than one definition URI is a reasonable traceability improvement, especially where an item relates to multiple formal sources. The change widens the base cardinality and does not invalidate R4 instances. The break described here is a downgrade and model-shape concern, so the backward-compatible alternative question is not applicable for R4-to-R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping `item.definition` at `0..1` and placing extra definitions in an extension would make downgrade easier, but the R6 change does not need such an alternative to preserve R4-valid instances. The material tradeoff is for R6 authors and R4 downgrades: multiple R6 values require either loss, rejection, or an extension convention when converted back to R4.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade and generated scalar models need policy for multiple definitions, but that is not a forward compatibility alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 max cardinality is 1.
R6 max cardinality is *.

examples.examplesMd: A downgrade must choose one definition, join values in a non-standard way, or use an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `item.definition` changed from scalar to repeatable. This is not a forward validation break, but it is a classic code-generation and downgrade break because the property shape changes from one URI to an array of URIs.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances with zero or one definition remain structurally compatible. R6 instances with two or more definitions are invalid in R4. Generated serializers, object mappers, and database schemas should update from scalar to collection.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, wrap the old scalar in a list in generated models. For R6-to-R4, decide whether to keep the primary definition, preserve extras with extensions, or reject lossy conversion.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been extension-based, but the base cardinality better supports multiple formal definitions. Downgrade remains inherently lossy without an extension convention.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Increasing `item.definition` from single-valued to repeatable is a widening. Existing R4 instances with zero or one URI still fit R6; only R6 authors who use multiple definitions, and R4 scalar generated models, need conversion policy.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.item.definition is 0..1 uri.
R6 Questionnaire.item.definition is 0..* uri.
R6 definition text also broadens the described target from ElementDefinition to ElementDefinition or ObservationDefinition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use calls for attention to migration burden, but this widening does not violate the stability expectation for existing R4 instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: multiple R6 definition values cannot be represented in R4 core; no R4 instance becomes invalid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping 0..1 and using an extension for extra definitions would ease downgrade, but it is not needed to preserve R4-valid content and would make the R6 traceability improvement less usable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing medium-impact framing as a fresh standards concern; agree that no forward less-breaking alternative is necessary.

findings.title: Questionnaire.item.answerOption.value[x] accepts additional datatypes in R6

oldState.summary: Allowed integer, date, time, string, Coding, and Reference(Resource).
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 answer options could not be decimal, dateTime, uri, or Quantity in the core element.

newState.summary: Adds decimal, dateTime, uri, and Quantity profiled to SimpleQuantity.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows enumerated answer options for more concrete answer datatypes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The widened type list does not invalidate old R4 content, but R6 questionnaires can now use answerOption values that R4 schemas and generated classes do not support. Downgrading those options requires extensions, conversion to strings/codings, or data loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow enumerated answer options for datatypes already used by questionnaire items and responses.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding answerOption value types widens the R6 type domain and preserves R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of supporting enumerated options for additional answer datatypes is reasonable and internally consistent with broader Questionnaire item typing. Since no R4 answerOption value type is removed, R4-valid instances remain valid in this respect. The compatibility concern is R6-to-R4 conversion of newly expressible content, so the alternative availability judgment is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: An extension-only approach could have carried decimal, dateTime, uri, or SimpleQuantity options in R4, but that is a downgrade or backport strategy. For the R6 base design, the widened type list is not a forward-breaking change that requires a less-breaking alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: New R6 option datatypes are not losslessly R4-representable, but that is a downgrade issue rather than a less-breaking forward design issue.

evidence.detail: R4 type list lacks decimal, dateTime, uri, and Quantity.
R6 type list adds decimal, dateTime, uri, and Quantity constrained to SimpleQuantity.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no `answerOption.valueDecimal`; representing it as a string or coding changes the datatype.

findings.narrativeMd: `answerOption.value[x]` is widened. This is beneficial for R6 authoring but creates round-trip and generated-model risk for systems built around the R4 choice set.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for existing answerOption values. R6-to-R4 is not lossless for the newly allowed datatypes. Strict R4 parsers will reject JSON properties such as `valueDecimal`, `valueDateTime`, `valueUri`, or `valueQuantity` under answerOption.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading, prefer preserving unsupported answer options in extensions rather than coercing to strings unless the receiving system explicitly accepts that semantic loss. Add test cases for every new answerOption datatype used by authored questionnaires.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been extension-only, but core support for these option datatypes is more consistent with R6 item typing. The backward-compatible alternative would have left common numeric and date/time enumerations awkward to model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `answerOption.value[x]` choice is widened. R4 answer options remain valid in R6, while new R6 decimal, dateTime, uri, or SimpleQuantity options are simply not native R4 content.
keyEvidence: R4 answerOption.value[x] allowed integer, date, time, string, Coding, and Reference(Resource).
R6 retains those types and adds decimal, dateTime, uri, and Quantity profiled to SimpleQuantity.
The element cardinality remains 1..1 in both versions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: For FMM 3/trial-use content, widening a choice type does not create a forward stability issue; downgrade limitations are expected for newly expressible R6 data.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 valueDecimal, valueDateTime, valueUri, and valueQuantity options are not valid R4 answerOption branches; no old-valid/new-invalid path exists.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed because the change is additive. Extension-only support would reduce interoperability without preserving additional R4 instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree that R6-to-R4 representability is real, but disagree that this widening is a meaningful R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: enableWhen answers add uri and Attachment while Quantity choices are constrained to SimpleQuantity

oldState.summary: enableWhen.answer[x] allowed Quantity without a SimpleQuantity profile and did not allow uri or Attachment. initial.value[x] also allowed unprofiled Quantity.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 quantity answers could include `Quantity.comparator`, because the choice type was unprofiled Quantity.

newState.summary: enableWhen.answer[x] adds uri and Attachment and profiles Quantity to SimpleQuantity; initial.value[x] profiles Quantity to SimpleQuantity.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits URI and attachment enableWhen comparisons but disallows comparator-bearing quantities in enableWhen and initial values through SimpleQuantity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Comparator-bearing R4 `valueQuantity` content in `enableWhen.answer[x]` or `initial.value[x]` can be invalid in R6 because R6 profiles those choices to SimpleQuantity. Separately, R6 `valueUri` and `valueAttachment` enableWhen answers are not valid R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Questionnaire quantity answers with SimpleQuantity and support additional comparison datatypes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep unprofiled Quantity in the base while adding guidance or warnings against comparator use.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added uri and Attachment branches are forward-compatible widenings, but profiling Quantity to SimpleQuantity can invalidate R4 comparator-bearing quantities. The R6 goal of deterministic enableWhen and initial-value semantics is reasonable. A less-breaking Quantity design exists, but it would either tolerate ambiguous comparisons such as `<5 mg` in form logic or force every renderer to implement extra comparator interpretation. Those material tradeoffs make the break probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have left `enableWhen.answerQuantity` and `initial.valueQuantity` as unprofiled Quantity and introduced warnings, best-practice guidance, or explicit comparator semantics. That would preserve more R4 instances. It is incomplete because warning-only validation does not prevent ambiguous executable logic, while defining comparator behavior would add implementation burden and potential safety risk.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves comparator-bearing R4 quantities but leaves ambiguous executable comparison semantics or requires all implementations to define comparator behavior.

evidence.detail: R4 includes unprofiled Quantity and does not include uri or Attachment.
R6 includes uri and Attachment and constrains Quantity to SimpleQuantity.
R6 constrains initial.valueQuantity to SimpleQuantity.
SimpleQuantity sets Quantity.comparator max to 0.

examples.examplesMd: The R4-to-R6 example relies on R4 allowing unprofiled Quantity in initial values. The R6-to-R4 example uses `answerUri`, which R4 enableWhen does not support.

findings.narrativeMd: This choice-type change has two directions. R6 broadens `enableWhen.answer[x]` with `uri` and `Attachment`, but it narrows Quantity choices for both enableWhen answers and initial values by requiring SimpleQuantity.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Quantity values with comparators can become invalid in R6 where SimpleQuantity applies. R6 URI or Attachment enableWhen answers cannot be expressed in R4 core. Generated choice accessors also change because R6 has additional `answerUri`/`answerAttachment` branches.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit `initial.valueQuantity` and `enableWhen.answerQuantity` for `comparator`. If present, remove or convert only with clinical/business review. For R6-to-R4, preserve URI/Attachment enablement conditions with extensions or reject downgrade if behavior must remain executable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrowing to SimpleQuantity is arguably justified to avoid comparator ambiguity in questionnaire logic, but it could have been introduced as a warning first. The uri/Attachment additions are backward-compatible forward but not backward-representable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The uri and Attachment branches are additive. The real break is that Quantity answers and initial values are now SimpleQuantity, so an R4 comparator-bearing Quantity can fail R6. That is a proportionate computability tradeoff because comparators in executable enableWhen logic or initial defaults are hard to interpret consistently.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.item.enableWhen.answer[x] includes unprofiled Quantity and lacks uri and Attachment.
R6 enableWhen.answer[x] adds uri and Attachment and profiles Quantity to SimpleQuantity.
R6 Questionnaire.item.initial.value[x] also profiles Quantity to SimpleQuantity; SimpleQuantity sets Quantity.comparator max to 0.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises concern for hard validator breaks, but the affected comparator pattern is narrower than the common Questionnaire paths and has a plausible safety/computability rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 valueQuantity content with comparator under enableWhen.answer or initial.value can fail R6 validation; added uri and Attachment branches are R6-to-R4 loss only.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep unprofiled Quantity and warn on comparator use. That would preserve more R4 instances but would leave ambiguous comparison and defaulting semantics for form engines.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing hard-break and partial-alternative assessment; the overall impact seems narrower than high unless comparator-bearing quantities are common locally.

findings.title: Questionnaire.item.linkId now rejects leading/trailing and non-single-space whitespace

oldState.summary: No local whitespace or length invariant on linkId.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required a linkId but did not constrain whitespace beyond being a string.

newState.summary: Adds error que-16 for whitespace shape and warning que-15 for length <=255.

constraints.human: LinkId cannot have leading or trailing spaces or intervening whitespace other than single space characters
Link ids should be 255 characters or less

newState.narrativeMd: R6 still allows spaces and slashes by design, but not leading/trailing spaces, tabs, newlines, or repeated whitespace runs.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with linkIds containing leading/trailing whitespace, tabs, newlines, or multiple adjacent whitespace characters can become invalid in R6. Long linkIds become warning-level conformance issues rather than hard validation failures.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Changing linkIds can break QuestionnaireResponse linkage, extraction maps, and enableWhen.question references.

justification.inferredGoal: Make linkIds more interoperable while still allowing meaningful whitespace and slashes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Stage the whitespace rule as a warning or best-practice invariant instead of an error.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Constraining hard-to-see whitespace in `linkId` is a reasonable interoperability goal because linkIds are used as stable join keys. A warning-only rule would avoid old-valid/new-invalid failures, but it would not prevent conformant R6 questionnaires from continuing to use identifiers that are easy to trim, collide, or mis-reference. Because those risks are real and the alternative is incomplete, the hard error is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made the new pattern warning-only for at least one release. That would preserve R4 questionnaires with leading, trailing, tab, newline, or repeated whitespace in linkIds. The tradeoff is that consumers would still need to accept and faithfully preserve visually ambiguous identifiers, and any later normalization could break `enableWhen.question`, `QuestionnaireResponse.item.linkId`, extraction logic, and external references.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old linkIds but leaves invisible or fragile identifiers in conformant data and complicates references, responses, and extraction maps.

evidence.detail: R6 adds an error invariant requiring a no-leading/trailing/single-space whitespace pattern.
R6 adds a warning recommending linkId length <=255.

examples.examplesMd: Renaming linkIds is not local to Questionnaire if responses or logic already reference them.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens `linkId` lexical validity. This is a small schema change with outsized migration risk because linkId is the join key between Questionnaire items, QuestionnaireResponse items, enableWhen rules, and extraction logic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs for whitespace forms newly rejected by que-16. R6-to-R4 is not a problem for valid R6 linkIds. Generated code is unaffected, but validators and migration scripts must normalize carefully.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Detect invalid linkIds, choose stable replacements, and update every internal and external reference. Do not trim silently unless you can prove no collisions are introduced after normalization.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rule could have been warning-only for one release. Making it an error improves interoperability but creates hard failures for existing questionnaires with visually ambiguous IDs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `linkId` is the stable join key between Questionnaire items, responses, conditional logic, and extraction artifacts. The R6 whitespace rule has a sensible interoperability goal, but making it an error immediately can force coordinated renames for strings that were R4-valid. A warning-first rule would expose the issue without breaking existing identifiers.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.item.linkId is required string with no local whitespace invariant.
R6 adds que-16 as an error: LinkId cannot have leading or trailing spaces or intervening whitespace other than single spaces.
R6 also adds que-15 as a warning for linkId length <=255.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use gives this central linkage field a meaningful stability expectation even though Questionnaire is not normative.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 linkIds with leading or trailing whitespace, tabs, newlines, or repeated whitespace can fail R6 validation; renaming affects downstream references.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could make the whitespace rule warning-level for a transition or best-practice period. The tradeoff is continued acceptance of fragile identifiers, but that seems lower cost than immediate hard failure on a central key.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment; I escalate to Revisit because the warning-level alternative is modest and the path is central.

findings.title: Exactly two enableWhen clauses now require enableBehavior

oldState.summary: R4 que-12 expression required enableBehavior only when enableWhen.count() > 2.
oldState.narrativeMd: Despite R4 human text saying more than one enableWhen, the computable expression only fired for three or more repetitions.

newState.summary: R6 que-12 expression requires enableBehavior when enableWhen.count() > 1.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes the computable invariant match the intended rule for any multiple enableWhen clauses and adds a warning that referenced questions should exist.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A Questionnaire item with exactly two enableWhen repetitions and no enableBehavior can validate in R4 but fail the R6 error invariant. This can change rendering behavior because `all` versus `any` is ambiguous without enableBehavior.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a warning-only rule or define a default enableBehavior for exactly two enableWhen clauses.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is to make multiple enableWhen conditions deterministic. This appears to fix the R4 computable expression so it matches the human rule for more than one condition. Although less-breaking alternatives exist, they fail the core safety goal: a warning preserves ambiguity, and a default may silently render or suppress items contrary to author intent. A hard validation error is therefore justified despite the Partial alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept the R4 `> 2` threshold, warned for exactly two clauses, or specified an implicit default when `enableBehavior` is absent. Those options preserve more R4 instances, but none is fully satisfactory. Warning-only validation leaves implementations to guess, while an implicit default can be clinically or operationally wrong when the author intended the opposite `all` or `any` behavior.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Warning-only leaves conditional logic ambiguous; defaulting to all or any can silently change runtime behavior for forms that intended the other meaning.

evidence.detail: R4 expression uses > 2.
R6 expression uses > 1.
R6 adds a warning that referenced questions should exist.

examples.examplesMd: The correct migration value may be `all` or `any`; it cannot always be inferred from the instance.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens conditional-display logic by requiring `enableBehavior` for two enableWhen clauses, not just three or more. This removes an ambiguity but breaks instances that relied on the R4 computable gap.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs for exactly two enableWhen repetitions without enableBehavior. R6 valid instances with explicit enableBehavior remain valid in R4. Runtime renderers must not guess `all` or `any` during migration without review.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Find items with `enableWhen.count() == 2` and missing `enableBehavior`. Set the value based on author intent, renderer behavior, or local profile rules. Also review new R6 warnings for enableWhen.question references that do not match a local linkId.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A default would have preserved validation but could silently change form behavior. Requiring the author to choose is safer for clinical and business logic.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The threshold change closes an R4 computable-invariant gap. Exactly two enableWhen conditions without enableBehavior were structurally valid under the R4 expression, but the runtime meaning is ambiguous; requiring the author to choose all or any is safer than silent defaulting.
keyEvidence: R4 que-12 expression is enableWhen.count() > 2 implies enableBehavior.exists().
R6 que-12 expression is enableWhen.count() > 1 implies enableBehavior.exists().
R6 also adds a warning on enableWhen.question references that do not match a linkId.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes the hard break worth noting, but the affected instances encode ambiguous conditional behavior and the R6 requirement is proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an item with exactly two enableWhen repetitions and no enableBehavior can pass R4 validation and fail R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-only rule or implicit default would preserve more instances, but warning leaves runtime ambiguity and defaulting to all or any can change form behavior contrary to author intent.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact, partial-alternative, and justified-break assessment.

findings.title: R6 enforces answerOption/initial type alignment and limits selected defaults for non-repeating items

oldState.summary: R4 comments said value datatypes should agree with item.type, but no local error invariant enforced this; multiple initialSelected options on non-repeating items were not locally prohibited.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators using only computable invariants could accept inconsistent answerOption or initial value datatypes.

newState.summary: Adds error invariants que-18a, que-18b, and que-17.

constraints.human: The types of any specified answerOptions must align with the item type
The types of any specified initial values must align with the item type
If question is non-repeating, cannot have more than one initialSelected answer option

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes several previously textual correctness expectations computable validation errors.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 Questionnaires with mismatched answerOption or initial datatypes, or multiple selected default options on non-repeating items, can become invalid in R6. These instances were already semantically suspicious, but the validation mechanism changes from prose/comment to hard invariant.

justification.inferredGoal: Prevent internally inconsistent questionnaires from validating.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the new alignment and initialSelected rules first as warnings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of preventing answerOption and initial-value type mismatches is reasonable because such forms can fail at rendering or response validation time. A staged warning would reduce immediate breakage, but it would continue to allow base-conformant questionnaires whose answers do not match their declared item type or whose defaults are inconsistent with non-repeating behavior. With those material tradeoffs and no official rationale reviewed, the hard invariants are probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have added warning-level invariants before making these conditions errors. That would preserve R4 instances that are structurally valid but semantically inconsistent. The alternative is incomplete because renderers, validators, and QuestionnaireResponse producers would still need local policies for mismatched answer datatypes and multiple selected defaults on non-repeating questions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves structurally valid but internally inconsistent R4 forms, forcing renderers and responders to handle ambiguous or impossible defaults.

evidence.detail: R6 adds answerOption type-alignment error.
R6 adds initial value type-alignment error.
R6 adds non-repeating initialSelected cardinality error.

examples.examplesMd: R4 comments discouraged this, but the base R4 StructureDefinition did not include the R6 error invariants.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 turns several consistency expectations into formal validation rules. This is likely to catch bad forms, but it is still a breaking change for systems that previously accepted or generated structurally valid but semantically inconsistent R4 questionnaires.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid depends on whether the R4 validator enforced comments or only constraints. Strict R6 validation fails the listed inconsistency patterns. R6-to-R4 is not materially risky because R4 can carry the same elements if they satisfy the stricter rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Run R6 validation over existing questionnaires and fix the actual datatype or item.type mismatch rather than suppressing errors. For multiple selected defaults, either set `repeats=true` if multiple answers are intended or keep only the single intended default.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The constraints are justified because they prevent forms that renderers cannot safely execute. A less-breaking staged warning would help migration, but would delay enforcement of real semantic errors.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The new invariants reject internally inconsistent forms: answer options or initial values whose datatypes do not match `item.type`, and multiple selected defaults for a non-repeating question. Those patterns may have been structurally accepted by R4 validators, but they are already problematic for renderers and response validation.
keyEvidence: R6 adds que-18a error for answerOption value type alignment.
R6 adds que-18b error for initial value type alignment.
R6 adds que-17 error limiting initialSelected options to one when repeats is false.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the burden for new errors, but the affected content is semantically inconsistent rather than a clean legacy modeling pattern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with mismatched answerOption or initial datatypes, or multiple selected defaults on non-repeating items, can fail R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-first stage is possible, but it would continue to declare executable questionnaires conformant even when their declared answer type and defaults disagree.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment; the break appears proportionate.

findings.title: Allowed contexts for answerValueSet and maxLength changed

oldState.summary: R4 que-5 allowed answerValueSet/answerOption for choice, open-choice, decimal, integer, date, dateTime, time, string, and quantity; que-10 allowed maxLength for boolean, decimal, integer, string, text, url, and open-choice.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed value sets on several non-coded primitive/quantity item types and allowed maxLength on boolean and open-choice.

newState.summary: R6 separates answerOption and answerValueSet rules; answerValueSet is effectively limited to coding, string, and uri. maxLength is allowed for string-like/date-time/numeric primitives or when answerConstraint is optionsOrString.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 narrows `answerValueSet` contexts but broadens some `maxLength` contexts for date/time values. Migrating old `open-choice` with maxLength requires setting `answerConstraint=optionsOrString`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using answerValueSet on decimal, integer, date, dateTime, time, or quantity items can become invalid in R6. R4 boolean maxLength can also become invalid. R6 instances using the newly allowed maxLength contexts or uri answerValueSet may not round-trip to R4 without adjustment.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify how enumerated answers and maximum lengths apply to each item datatype.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old answerValueSet and maxLength contexts with warnings and clearer definitions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of clarifying where answer value sets and maximum lengths are meaningful is reasonable. A less-breaking design could have tolerated the R4 contexts, but the old rules allowed patterns whose semantics are difficult to interpret consistently across validators and renderers. Because retaining them would carry ongoing ambiguity and implementation cost, the stricter R6 constraints are probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept the R4-permitted contexts for `answerValueSet` and `maxLength` while warning when the semantics are questionable. That would preserve questionnaires using primitive, date/time, quantity, or boolean patterns now rejected by R6. The tradeoff is that base R6 would continue to allow answer-set and length rules whose interpretation is unclear or inconsistent, shifting the burden to profiles and implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves older modeling patterns but keeps ambiguous terminology semantics for numeric, date/time, and quantity answers and odd length semantics such as boolean maxLength.

evidence.detail: R4 que-5 allowed answerValueSet or answerOption on choice/open-choice and several primitive/quantity types.
R6 que-5b limits answerValueSet contexts.
R4 que-10 allowed boolean and open-choice maxLength.
R6 que-10 changes maxLength contexts and depends on answerConstraint for open-choice migration.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows the coupled requirement for old open-choice items that used maxLength.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes the rules around where enumerated answer value sets and length limits are valid. These are local Questionnaire invariants, so they can make previously accepted R4 forms fail even though no element was removed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs for the narrowed answerValueSet contexts and boolean maxLength. R6-to-R4 issues occur for contexts newly allowed in R6. The most important migration trap is `open-choice`: converting only to `coding` while keeping `maxLength` fails unless `answerConstraint=optionsOrString` is also set.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review all items with `answerValueSet` and non-coding/string types. Consider replacing finite primitive/date/quantity value sets with explicit `answerOption` values where R6 supports them, or use profiles/extensions if a terminology server expansion remains necessary. For maxLength, remove it from boolean items and preserve old open-choice behavior with `answerConstraint=optionsOrString`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 constraints could have been softer warnings for one release, but they reduce ambiguity in how terminology-based options apply to non-coded answers. Migration should be explicit because automatic coercion can change valid answer sets.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is more than a harmless cleanup. R6 narrows `answerValueSet` contexts and changes `maxLength` rules, and the checked R6 `que-10` expression appears to use `optionOrString` even though the allowed answerConstraint code is `optionsOrString`. That mismatch undermines the obvious migration path for old open-choice items with maxLength and should be corrected or staged.
keyEvidence: R4 que-5 allowed answerValueSet or answerOption for choice, open-choice, decimal, integer, date, dateTime, time, string, and quantity.
R6 que-5b expression allows answerValueSet only when type is coding, string, or uri.
R4 que-10 allowed maxLength for boolean, decimal, integer, string, text, url, and open-choice.
R6 que-10 expression checked locally uses answerConstraint='optionOrString', while questionnaire-answer-constraint defines optionsOrString.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes hard narrowing of existing validation contexts significant, and the apparent invariant/code mismatch weakens confidence that the R6 design is ready as-is.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 forms using answerValueSet on now-disallowed item types, boolean maxLength, or open-choice maxLength migration patterns can fail R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could retain former contexts as warnings while clarifying semantics, and the optionOrString/optionsOrString mismatch looks like a low-cost fix. Retaining every old context has ambiguity costs, but the current rule set needs standards attention.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment, but disagree with treating the change as probably justified without addressing the primary-evidence mismatch.

findings.title: R6 allows inactive empty groups as warning-only, but R4 rejects them

oldState.summary: R4 que-1 required all group items to have nested items as an error.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, an empty group is invalid regardless of Questionnaire.status.

newState.summary: R6 makes empty groups an error only when Questionnaire.status is active and a warning otherwise.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits draft, retired, or unknown questionnaires with empty groups to pass error-level validation, while still warning.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 break; it is a downgrade break. An R6 draft/retired/unknown Questionnaire with an empty group can be error-valid in R6 but invalid in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow incomplete non-active questionnaires during authoring while keeping active questionnaires strict.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 relaxes empty-group validation for non-active questionnaires and does not break R4-to-R6 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: draft, retired, or otherwise non-active questionnaires may be incomplete during authoring. Since this change weakens an R4 error for non-active resources, it does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6. The issue is a pure downgrade concern, so backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable under the calibration rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the R4 error for all statuses would avoid this R6-to-R4 downgrade mismatch, but that is not a less-breaking alternative for R4-to-R6 compatibility because R6 is relaxing the rule. Downgrade tools still need to reject, remove, fill, or extension-preserve inactive empty groups when producing valid R4.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The compatibility cost is R6-to-R4 downgrade handling for draft or inactive empty groups, not a less-breaking forward R6 design choice.

evidence.detail: R4 has a single error requiring group items to have children.
R6 splits the rule into active-only error and general warning.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is warning-level non-conformant but not error-invalid under the R6 base invariant; R4 rejects it as an error.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 weakens the empty-group rule for non-active questionnaires. This matters mostly for authoring repositories that downgrade draft forms to R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 migration is not broken by this change. R6-to-R4 conversion must add at least one child item, remove the empty group, change the status/validation mode, or reject downgrade.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before downgrading R6 questionnaires, scan non-active forms for group items without children. Decide whether to remove placeholder groups or keep them with an extension/private authoring representation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 relaxation is understandable for draft authoring. It could have been confined to tooling profiles, but adding status-sensitive behavior to the base invariant makes authoring-state semantics explicit.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 relaxes the empty-group rule for non-active questionnaires. That cannot make R4-valid content invalid in R6; it only means an R6 draft or inactive placeholder group may need action before downgrade to R4.
keyEvidence: R4 que-1 is an error requiring group items to have nested items.
R6 que-1a makes the empty-group error apply when Questionnaire.status is active.
R6 que-1b keeps a general warning that groups should have items.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not raise a forward compatibility concern for a relaxation; the only burden is downgrade policy for R6 authoring states.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: a non-active R6 Questionnaire with an empty group can avoid an R6 error but fail R4 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking forward R6 design is needed. Keeping the R4 error for all statuses would reduce downgrade mismatch but would remove the R6 authoring-state relaxation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing medium-impact framing as an R4-to-R6 concern; agree that no backward-compatible alternative is applicable.

findings.title: R6 adds Questionnaire.item.disabledDisplay for rendering disabled items

oldState.summary: No core element specified whether disabled enableWhen-controlled items should be hidden or visible but protected.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 renderers used local conventions or extensions for disabled item display.

newState.summary: Optional code element with required binding hidden|protected.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 gives authors a standard way to specify disabled item rendering behavior.

facts.newValue: Controls display of items disabled by enableWhen.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R6 instances using `disabledDisplay` cannot be represented in R4 core. R4 renderers or downgraded forms that ignore it may hide information that should remain visible or expose controls that should be protected.

justification.inferredGoal: Standardize rendering behavior for disabled questionnaire items.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional disabledDisplay does not invalidate R4 Questionnaire instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing disabled-item rendering behavior is a reasonable R6 goal. Because `disabledDisplay` is optional and newly added, existing R4 questionnaires can remain valid when interpreted as R6 with respect to this element. The compatibility concern is lossless R6-to-R4 representation and renderer behavior, so a backward-compatible alternative judgment is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed for forward instance compatibility. An R4 extension can preserve `disabledDisplay` during downgrade, but that is a conversion strategy. Leaving the concept extension-only in R6 would reduce standard renderer interoperability without preserving any R4 instance that the optional element would otherwise break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Populated R6 disabledDisplay values require downgrade policy, but extension/backport preservation is a mitigation rather than a base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds disabledDisplay 0..1 with required binding hidden|protected.
The R6 code system defines hidden and protected.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no native disabledDisplay element; an extension is needed for lossless downgrade.

findings.narrativeMd: `disabledDisplay` is not a validation break for old data, but it is a runtime interoperability change. It affects what users see and can edit when enableWhen disables an item.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is safe because the element is optional. R6-to-R4 is not lossless when the element is populated. Runtime renderers need to honor `hidden` versus `protected` to preserve author intent.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For downgrade, carry `disabledDisplay` in a cross-version extension or document a renderer-specific policy. Test conditional-display forms with both `hidden` and `protected` behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A standard element is justified for renderer interoperability, but R4 systems need an extension convention to preserve the behavior.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `disabledDisplay` is an optional R6 element for renderer behavior. It creates a downgrade and rendering consideration when populated, but it does not invalidate existing R4 questionnaires or remove an R4 representation.
keyEvidence: R4 has no Questionnaire.item.disabledDisplay element.
R6 adds Questionnaire.item.disabledDisplay 0..1 code.
R6 questionnaire-disabled-display CodeSystem defines hidden and protected.
freshReview.fmmEffect: For FMM 3/trial-use content, an optional additive rendering control is not a forward compatibility break, though implementers should document downgrade behavior.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: populated disabledDisplay has no R4 core field; no old-valid/new-invalid mechanism exists.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base alternative is needed. Extension-only support would avoid native R6-to-R4 loss but would also forgo a standard R6 renderer signal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing medium-impact framing for this path-level finding; agree that a less-breaking base alternative is not applicable.

findings.title: Questionnaire.description and Questionnaire.derivedFrom are now summary elements

oldState.summary: description and derivedFrom were not summary elements in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 summary serialization did not include these local Questionnaire metadata fields by default.

newState.summary: description and derivedFrom have isSummary=true in R6; new versionAlgorithm[x] is also summary.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 summary views can include more Questionnaire metadata and derivation information.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not change instance validity, but REST `_summary`, generated summary serializers, search result payloads, and cache keys may include additional local Questionnaire metadata in R6.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose useful metadata in summary views.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: changing summary flags does not invalidate R4 Questionnaire instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of exposing useful Questionnaire description and derivation metadata in summary views is reasonable, and the change does not affect full-resource instance validity. Under this calibration, the finding is a runtime projection compatibility concern rather than a breaking R4-to-R6 base instance-design issue. The backward-compatible alternative availability judgment is therefore not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A server or client can use `_elements` or other explicit projection controls when it needs stable summary payloads, but that is operational mitigation. Because no R4 instance becomes invalid and no R4 element representation is removed or narrowed, there is no less-breaking base R6 instance-design alternative to assess.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Runtime summary projections may include more metadata; clients needing fixed payloads can request explicit elements, but this is not an R4-to-R6 instance-shape alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 does not mark these two local elements as summary.
R6 marks description and derivedFrom as summary.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON validity example is needed because summary flags affect serialization modes, not instance shape.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes summary-serialization behavior for local Questionnaire metadata. This is a runtime/API compatibility concern rather than a data validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Full-resource instances remain valid. Clients using `_summary=true`, generated summary projections, or payload-size assumptions may see extra fields in R6 responses.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review any code that compares summary payloads, calculates cache signatures, or assumes summary responses omit description/derivedFrom. Use `_elements` for stable field selection if necessary.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is low risk and likely useful, but it is not fully backward-compatible for clients that treat summary payload shape as fixed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Changing summary flags affects projection behavior, not instance validity. R6 summary responses may include more Questionnaire metadata, but full-resource content and validation are unchanged.
keyEvidence: R4 Questionnaire.description and Questionnaire.derivedFrom have isSummary=false.
R6 Questionnaire.description and Questionnaire.derivedFrom have isSummary=true.
R6 also adds versionAlgorithm[x] as a summary element.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use has little effect here because the change is metadata/API projection behavior rather than a structural or semantic validation break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: clients using _summary or generated summary projections may see extra fields; there is no instance-shape break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No base instance-design alternative is needed. Clients that require fixed projections can request explicit elements, but that is operational mitigation rather than a different R6 model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree that the impact is low and that no less-breaking base alternative is applicable.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, and abstract flag are stable. R6 status changed to active, noted as non-breaking.
No local Questionnaire element IDs present in R4 were removed in R6. R6 adds optional local elements, which are covered in findings or notable changes.
No local min cardinality increases or max decreases were found. The material max increase for `item.definition` is reported as a finding.
`derivedFrom` still targets Questionnaire and local Reference(Resource) target profiles on choice elements remain Resource where present.
Status, enableWhen.operator, and enableBehavior code systems appear materially unchanged apart from version pins. Material binding changes for item.type and subjectType are reported.
No local fixed, pattern, or defaultValue changes were identified on Questionnaire elements.
No local slicing changes were identified in the Questionnaire StructureDefinition.
Local modifier flags for `status` and `item.enableWhen` remain modifier elements. Inherited modifierExtension summary/constraint differences were treated as out of scope.
No local type removals were found. Material type additions/profile narrowings on answer choices are reported.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds versionAlgorithm[x]
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional, so existing R4 Questionnaire instances remain valid with respect to this addition.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 version comparison logic is not natively representable in R4. Downgrade can preserve it with an extension or omit it with documented loss.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds copyrightLabel
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The element is optional and does not affect R4-to-R6 validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6 renderers may display this footer label. R4 downgrade needs an extension or accepts loss of display metadata.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Jurisdiction binding URL moved and comments encourage useContext jurisdiction
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding remains extensible and the element shape is unchanged, so this is not a hard validation break for ordinary jurisdiction codings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: New authoring should consider representing jurisdiction through `useContext` with the jurisdiction usage-context type, as suggested by the R6 comment.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds or tightens warning-level canonical/name guidance
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Questionnaire.url` restriction on `|`, `#`, and spaces is warning-level, and the `name` regex change is also warning-level.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Quality gates that fail on warnings may need to remediate single-character names or canonical URLs containing problematic characters.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Questionnaire StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata about the definition artifact, not a JSON/XML instance content-model change.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance processes that filter artifacts by status may treat R6 Questionnaire differently.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Questionnaire item.type, answerConstraint, initial values, and answerOption changes should be reconciled with QuestionnaireResponse answer typing and validation.
Inherited language, modifierExtension, dom-* constraints, and base summary behavior were intentionally excluded here and should be covered by base artifact reports.
The local Questionnaire break for Quantity choices depends on SimpleQuantity prohibiting `Quantity.comparator`; datatype/profile analysis should confirm broader migration guidance.
Questionnaire.subjectType migration requires cross-version mappings for removed and added resource-type codes.
